ai.literal: Why do the eyes themselves weep now, when they themselves showed us that which caused this unceasing pain?
ai.translation: Why do my eyes weep now? It was they who showed me my lover, bringing upon me this unceasing pain of separation that I now suffer.
ai.modern: தவிர்க்க முடியாத இந்தக் காம நோயை, அன்று அவர்களே காட்டி இன்று நாம் அனுபவிப்பதற்குக் காரணமான கண்கள், இப்போது தாமே அழுவது ஏனோ?
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the distress of her eyes, which are weeping due to the pain of separation from her lover. She points out the irony of their tears: it was her eyes that eagerly looked upon her lover in the first place, initiating the love that led to this relentless affliction. Since the eyes themselves showed her the lover and invited this pain, she questions why they are now weeping as if they are innocent victims of their own actions.

ai.literal: Without discerningly understanding, the kohl-painted eyes which looked, now without being pitied and understood, why do they suffer distress?
ai.translation: Why do these kohl-painted eyes, which gazed at him without foreseeing the consequences, now suffer this distress when he does not pity or understand their pain?
ai.modern: விளைவை ஆராய்ந்து அறியாமல் அன்று காதலனைப் பார்த்த மைதீட்டிய கண்கள், இன்று அவர் இரங்கி அருள் செய்யாதபோது துன்பத்தை அனுபவிப்பது ஏன்?
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the state of her own eyes which are weeping due to separation from her lover. She addresses them with gentle irony, asking why they are suffering now. When they first eagerly looked at him, they did so blindly without discerning the future pain of parting (தெரிந்துணரா நோக்கிய). Now, when the lover is away and does not pity or understand their plight (பரிந்துணரா), the eyes endure deep sorrow (பைதல் உழப்பது). She highlights that the eyes brought this misery upon themselves by looking at him in the first place.

ai.translation: Having eagerly looked on their own, my eyes now weep by themselves; this is truly something to be laughed at.

ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks of the irony of her eyes' behavior. The eyes eagerly and hastily rushed to look at her lover when he was near. Now that he is away, those very same eyes weep in deep sorrow and longing. She remarks that this self-inflicted grief is highly amusing and worthy of mockery, as the eyes themselves brought about this pain by looking in the first place.

ai.translation: My collyrium-painted eyes, having run completely dry of tears from endless weeping, have now left an inescapable, incurable affliction within me.
ai.modern: தொடர்ந்து அழுது அழுது கண்ணீர் வற்றிப்போன என் மை தீட்டிய கண்கள், தப்பிக்கவே முடியாத தீராத துன்பத்தை என்னிடத்தில் நிலைநிறுத்திவிட்டன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the state of her eyes during separation from her lover. Her eyes wept so continuously that they have completely run out of tears ('நீருலந்த'). Having exhausted their ability to weep, these very eyes have now left her with an inescapable, incurable disease of love-sickness ('உய்வில்நோய்') inside her. The word 'உண்கண்' refers to eyes adorned with collyrium, highlighting their former beauty which is now ruined by endless grief.

ai.literal: Unable to endure closing, suffering grief, my eyes, which caused the love-sickness exceeding the ocean.
ai.translation: My very eyes, which brought upon me this love-sickness greater than the ocean, are now suffering from grief, unable even to close in sleep.
ai.modern: கடலை விடப் பெரிய காம நோயை எனக்கு உண்டாக்கிய என் கண்கள், இப்போது தூங்குவதற்குக் கூட முடியாமல் துன்பத்தை அனுபவிக்கின்றன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the irony of her situation. It was her own eyes that first gazed upon her lover and created a passion so vast that even the ocean cannot contain it (கடல் ஆற்றா காமநோய்). Now, those very same eyes are unable to close (படல் ஆற்றா) in sleep and must endure the agonizing grief of separation. The poet beautifully contrasts the active role of the eyes in creating the desire with their current passive suffering.

ai.explanation: The heroine speaks with bitter irony about her own eyes. They were the ones that first eagerly looked at her lover and brought this painful sickness of longing upon her. Now, because they cannot see him, they are weeping and suffering sleeplessly. She mockingly remarks that it is 'sweet' (இனிதே) to see the instigators of her pain suffering the very same fate they brought upon her.

ai.literal: Having suffered and suffered, let the inner water dry up, of the eyes that, having desired, wasted away, and wanted, saw him.
ai.translation: Let the tears within these eyes dry up completely after endless suffering, for they are the very eyes that eagerly desired, melted with love, and sought to look upon him.
ai.modern: விரும்பி, உருகி, அவரே வேண்டுமென்று அவரைப் பார்த்த கண்கள், இப்போது துன்பப்பட்டுத் துன்பப்பட்டுத் தங்களுக்குள் இருக்கும் கண்ணீர் வற்றிப் போகட்டும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine is expressing her frustration with her own eyes, which weep incessantly in the absence of her lover. She points out that it was her eyes that initially desired him, melted with love, and insisted on looking at him. Since they brought this longing upon themselves, she declares that they deserve to suffer and weep until their inner tears dry up completely. The repetition of 'uḻantu' emphasizes the intensity of the suffering, while 'iḻaintu' beautifully captures how the eyes (and the lover) waste away or melt in intense desire.

ai.literal: Without caring, he who loved exists indeed; but, him without seeing, rest do not have the eyes.
ai.translation: He who once loved me now lives without caring for me; yet, my eyes find no rest without seeing him.
ai.modern: என்னை விரும்பியவர் இப்போது என் மீது அன்பு செலுத்தாமல் வாழ்கிறார்; ஆயினும், என் கண்கள் அவரைக் காணாமல் அமைதி அடைவதில்லை.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments her helpless state to her companion. Her lover, who once cherished her deeply ('பெட்டார்'), now lives far away and seems completely indifferent to her suffering ('பேணாது உளர்'). Despite his cold neglect, her eyes refuse to cooperate with her mind; they cannot find any rest or stillness ('அமைவில') unless they see him ('காணாது'). This highlights the painful irony of love, where the physical senses continue to yearn intensely for the very person who has abandoned them.

ai.translation: When my lover does not come, my eyes do not sleep; even when he does come, they do not sleep. In either state, they suffer endless grief.
ai.modern: காதலர் வராதபோது கண்கள் தூங்குவதில்லை; அவர் வந்தபோதும் அவை தூங்குவதில்லை; இவ்விரண்டு நிலைகளிலும் என் கண்கள் மிகுந்த துன்பத்தையே அடைகின்றன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the constant distress of her eyes. When her lover is away, her eyes cannot sleep because of the painful longing of separation. When he returns, they still do not sleep because they fear losing sight of him even for a moment, or because they are too busy gazing at him. Thus, whether he is absent or present, her eyes find no rest and suffer continuous affliction.

ai.literal: Obtaining the secret is not difficult indeed to the townspeople, inside those who have eyes like a beaten drum like us.
ai.translation: It is not at all difficult for the townspeople to discover my secret, for my eyes act like a beaten drum, loudly proclaiming what is hidden within me.
ai.modern: எங்களைப் போல அடிக்கப்படும் பறை போன்ற கண்களை உடையவர்களின் உள்ளத்தில் உள்ள ரகசியத்தை அறிவது இவ்வூர் மக்களுக்கு அரிதானது அல்ல.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments that she cannot keep her love a secret from the villagers. She compares her eyes to a beaten drum, which by its very nature broadcasts news to the entire town. Just as a drumbeat makes a public announcement, her expressive and tearful eyes instantly reveal the secret longing of her heart. Therefore, the townspeople easily perceive the love she tries to hide.
